_title: The machine again, with a ROM where the matrix was
_description: The same computer as C10, running the same program to the same answer — and ten chips of control logic have become two EEPROMs. Load LDA 3, ADD 3, OUT and 5 into cells 0 to 3, clock, and the output lands on ten, exactly as before. The datapath below the control unit is C10's wire for wire; only how the control word is produced has changed. There is no decoder either, because a ROM does not need one: the opcode IS part of the address. What changes is what happens next — a matrix grows a gate per instruction, a ROM grows a row, and the instruction set becomes a file you can edit rather than a board you must rewire.
